candidates.name: Cindy Hyde-Smith
candidates.background: U.S. Senator since April 2018; cattle farmer, former Mississippi Commissioner of Agriculture and Commerce (2012-2018) and state senator (2000-2012), first elected as a Democrat before switching parties in 2010. Won the March 10, 2026 Republican primary with 80.8% over physician Sarah Adlakha; endorsed by President Trump.
priorities: Permanent extension of the 2017 tax cuts
Expanding Gulf offshore oil and gas production

cost.label: Answers family cost pressures with more supply, not caps: 'stop finding every excuse in the book to shrink energy production'; cosponsored the Lease Now Act to force resumed lease sales (Senate office)

health.label: Calls the ACA 'anything but affordable' and 'unsupportable over the long term'; instead of extending subsidies, backs S.3386 directing funds to patients rather than insurance companies (Senate office)

housing.label: Backs the ROAD to Housing Act to 'increase housing supply, cut regulations' and get 'the government out of the way' with no new federal spending (Senate office)

immigration.label: Voted to pass the Laken Riley Act, S. 5, requiring DHS detention of aliens charged with theft, passed 64-35 (Senate roll call 7, Jan 20, 2025)

taxes.label: Voted for the One Big Beautiful Bill Act making the 2017 tax cuts permanent, versus 'forcing a more than $4.0 trillion tax hike on everyone' (Senate office)

climate.label: Cosponsored the Offshore Energy Security Act of 2025 to resume Gulf of Mexico oil and gas lease sales, 'unleashing American energy dominance' (Senate office)

education.label: Cosponsored National School Choice Week resolutions: parents should be able to 'direct their children to schools that best suit their needs', including charter, private, online, and homeschool options (Senate office)

safety.label: Cosponsors the Back the Blue Act, S.3366, creating new federal crimes with mandatory sentences and death-penalty eligibility for killing officers: targeting police 'should be met with the full force of the law' (Senate office)

repro.label: Defended OBBBA language 'prohibiting abortion providers from receiving Medicaid funds' on the Senate floor, raising a point of order against the amendment to strike it (Congressional Record via Senate office)

democracy.label: Voted to sustain the objection to counting Arizona's 2020 electoral votes, one of 6 senators to do so, objection failed 6-93 (Senate roll call 1, Jan 6, 2021)

controversies.label: Her 2018 runoff remark 'if he invited me to a public hanging, I'd be in the front row' drew national criticism given Mississippi's lynching history; she called the criticism 'ridiculous' and did not apologize (Wikipedia)

candidates.name: Scott Colom
candidates.now: District Attorney, 16th Circuit Court District of Mississippi
candidates.background: District attorney for Mississippi's 16th Circuit (Lowndes, Clay, Noxubee, and Oktibbeha counties) since 2016, elected at 32 by defeating a nearly 30-year incumbent, the first Black DA elected in a majority-white Mississippi district. Nominated by President Biden to a federal judgeship in 2022 but blocked when Hyde-Smith withheld her blue slip. Won the March 10, 2026 Democratic primary with 73%, calling himself 'a commonsense Democrat with Mississippi values.'
priorities: Save Mississippi hospitals and reverse Medicaid cuts

cost.label: 'We got to raise the minimum wage. We haven't raised it, it's $7.25'; frames the race around lowering costs for families (Magnolia Tribune)

health.label: Medicaid expansion is 'a good deal for Mississippi'; says his first bill would 'cancel the healthcare cuts' from the One Big Beautiful Bill and restore ACA subsidies (Magnolia Tribune)

immigration.label: Mixed: supports a 'strong, secure border' but 'we also have to have due process' (Magnolia Tribune)

taxes.label: 'We have to raise taxes 3 percent on people making more than $600,000 a year to pay for Mississippians to continue to have health insurance, and to save our hospitals' (Magnolia Tribune)

education.label: Proposes teachers earning under $75,000 pay no federal income tax because Mississippi is 'losing too many teachers and cops' (Magnolia Tribune)

safety.label: Mixed record: convictions in over 95% of jury trials including high-profile murders, AND freed a man held 11 years without trial and dropped murder charges built on discredited bite-mark evidence (Wikipedia)

democracy.label: Mixed: open to voter ID if 'everybody needs to get access to a free ID very easily', while insisting polls stay 'available to people' (Magnolia Tribune)
